evidence: src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: execute() maps input.lines to domain values using Quantity.of. Validation stays in the domain.
execute() calls Order.place(this.ids.next(), input.customerId, lines, this.clock.now()). Order creation is handed to the domain factory.
execute() calls this.stock.reserve(order.lines) and this.orders.save(order) through injected domain ports and services. This is orchestration, which belongs in the application layer.
execute() returns toOrderDto(order), an application-layer DTO mapping. There is no HTTP, framework or database code.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: PlaceOrderUseCase.ts is a standard application-layer use case. It turns input into domain value objects (Quantity.of) and hands order creation to the domain factory Order.place. It then coordinates the domain services and ports it receives through the constructor (StockReservationService, OrderRepository, IdGenerator, Clock) and maps the result to a DTO. The file has no persistence code (it calls the save port but does not implement it), no transport or framework logic, and no business rules of its own. Invariants and business decisions stay in the domain. All of this matches the role of the application layer.
